status_label: Truce Holding — China 10% Levy May Lift Oct 1; USMCA Origin No Longer Shields
status_note:
WHAT APPLIES TODAY. US soybeans into China face roughly 13% (3% MFN + China's broad 10% 'Liberation Day' retaliatory levy); corn and wheat about 11%, pork about 22%. The March 2025 retaliatory tranche of up to 15% was lifted on Nov 10, 2025 under the Busan truce, which has been extended through Nov 10, 2026. A May 18, 2026 deal added at least $17B/yr of US ag purchases through 2028 on top of Busan's 25 MMT/yr of soybeans; as of Aug 10, 2026 China was roughly a quarter of the way through the 2026 soybean commitment — behind pace, with buying accelerating into an expected September Trump-Xi meeting.

THE ONE TO WATCH. On July 6, 2026 it was reported that the US would end its 10% fentanyl tariff and China would reciprocate by dropping its 10% levy on US ag, aimed at cargoes arriving after Oct 1, 2026. China's Ministry of Commerce confirmed it; USTR had not. That levy is the whole difference between 13% and 3% on soybeans, so treat the Oct 1 date as reported, not settled.

TARIFF AUTHORITY. SCOTUS voided the IEEPA tariffs on Feb 20, 2026. The Section 122 surcharge that replaced them was ruled invalid by the Court of International Trade on May 7, 2026 (under appeal) and lapsed around July 24. Section 301 'forced labor' duties took effect July 24, 2026 at 10-12.5% across 60 trading partners and about 99.4% of US imports, with a transit grace period to July 28. Farm inputs are explicitly exempt: in-quota sugar, fertilizer and pesticides, and certain planting seeds.

NORTH AMERICA. The Administration signalled in July that it will not renew USMCA and will negotiate a successor; bilateral talks resumed in Mexico City the week of Jul 20. Then in August the US imposed 50% Section 338 duties on about $20B of Canadian imports — dairy, alcoholic beverages and motor vehicles, with a covered list reaching honey, certain planting seeds, molasses and fructose syrups. Sources differ on the operative date (Aug 19 per counsel, 12:01 a.m. ET Aug 22 per customs brokers). Bulk grain and oilseeds are not covered, so the 0% rows above are unchanged — but USMCA origin did NOT exempt covered goods, which is the first outright override of USMCA duty-free treatment and it happened mid-renegotiation. Canada retaliated on Aug 25 with $27.6B in counter-tariffs: 50% on certain steel and aluminum, 25% on fish and tools. No bulk ag on either list.

UNCONFIRMED — one trade tracker lists a further Canadian counter-tariff tranche of 15-50% effective Sept 8, 2026. We found no second source and are not putting a number to it; if you ship to Canada, confirm directly.

BRAZIL. A 25% tariff on Brazilian goods including ethanol landed mid-July after a Section 301 investigation — an inbound tariff that structurally favours US corn ethanol at home.

Verify against USTR and the Federal Register before any trading decision.
headline: China's retained 10% levy still keeps US soybeans near 13%, but a reported deal would drop it for cargoes arriving after Oct 1. Section 301 forced-labor duties are in effect at 10-12.5% with fertilizer and pesticides exempt. New 50% Section 338 duties on Canadian dairy, alcohol and vehicles did NOT spare USMCA-originating goods — grain is untouched, but the precedent matters while USMCA is renegotiated.

rows.note: China lifted its March 2025 retaliatory 10% on soybeans under the Busan agreement (effective Nov 10, 2025) but kept its broad 10% 'Liberation Day' retaliatory levy — so US soybeans face roughly 13% (3% MFN + 10%), a persistent disadvantage vs. Brazil. A Section 301 investigation is pending and could re-escalate. Watch: a reported Jul 6 deal would drop this 10% for cargoes arriving after Oct 1 — China's MOFCOM confirmed it, USTR had not.

China suspended its March 2025 retaliatory 15% on corn under the Busan agreement but kept the broad 10% retaliatory levy, leaving roughly 11% (1% MFN + 10%). China purchases remain below pre-trade-war levels; Brazil retains market share. Watch: a reported Jul 6 deal would drop this 10% for cargoes arriving after Oct 1 — China's MOFCOM confirmed it, USTR had not.

March 2025 retaliatory 15% suspended under the Busan agreement; the broad 10% retaliatory levy remains (~11% = 1% MFN + 10%). US wheat has modest direct China exposure — global trade flows matter more than this rate. Watch: a reported Jul 6 deal would drop this 10% for cargoes arriving after Oct 1 — China's MOFCOM confirmed it, USTR had not.

March 2025 retaliatory 10% suspended under the Busan agreement; the broad 10% retaliatory levy remains (~22% = 12% MFN + 10%). China resumed US beef and poultry access under the May 18, 2026 deal and remains a major US pork market. Watch: a reported Jul 6 deal would drop this 10% for cargoes arriving after Oct 1 — China's MOFCOM confirmed it, USTR had not.

USMCA-compliant, duty-free. USMCA joint review underway (US-Mexico bilateral rounds began May 2026). Penn Wharton: USMCA exemption share reached 86.3% of Canada/Mexico imports by February 2026. USMCA renegotiation opened July 2026 — rates unchanged so far, but the framework itself is now in play. Aug 2026: 50% Section 338 duties on Canadian dairy, alcohol and vehicles applied DESPITE USMCA origin. Grain is not covered and this rate is unchanged.

USMCA-compliant, duty-free. Mexico remains the top US corn export destination; Canadian demand steady. USMCA joint review underway. USMCA renegotiation opened July 2026 — rates unchanged so far, but the framework itself is now in play. Aug 2026: 50% Section 338 duties on Canadian dairy, alcohol and vehicles applied DESPITE USMCA origin. Grain is not covered and this rate is unchanged.

No EU anti-dumping duty on US ethanol. The 2013 duty was repealed by Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2019/765, in force 16 May 2019, and the proceeding was terminated. What remains is the ordinary Common Customs Tariff import duty — €192/m³ undenatured, €102/m³ denatured — which applies EU-wide, not by member state. The Dutch RED III vote of Oct 2025 bars imported denatured ethanol from counting toward renewable-fuel obligations from 2026; that is a compliance rule, not a duty. The UK-US deal (May 2025) opened a 1.4B L/yr duty-free quota for the UK only. Verify member-state customs for specific shipments.

timeline.event: Canada retaliates with $27.6B in counter-tariffs: 50% on certain steel and aluminum, 25% on fish and tools. No bulk agricultural commodity is named in the Canadian list.

US imposes 50% Section 338 duties on roughly $20B of Canadian imports — dairy (notably TRQ cheese), alcoholic beverages and motor vehicles, plus a longer covered list that reaches honey, certain planting seeds, molasses and fructose syrups. Grain and oilseeds are NOT covered. The date differs by source: counsel reported it effective Aug 19, customs brokers put it at 12:01 a.m. ET Aug 22 for entries on or after that date — confirm the entry date for a specific shipment. Critically, USMCA origin does NOT exempt covered goods, which is the first time duty-free USMCA treatment has been overridden outright while the agreement is being renegotiated.

China is roughly a quarter of the way through its 25 MMT/yr soybean commitment for 2026 — behind pace with a Trump-Xi meeting expected in September. Buying accelerated into that meeting; private crushers reportedly held back.

Section 301 'forced labor' duties take effect at 10-12.5% across 60 trading partners, covering about 99.4% of US imports and replacing the lapsed Section 122 surcharge (goods in transit had a grace period to July 28). Agricultural exemptions apply universally to in-quota sugar, FERTILIZER AND PESTICIDES, and certain planting seeds — input costs are shielded. Five economies were cut to 10% after forced-labour import bans or trade commitments; the EU, Japan, South Korea, Switzerland and Taiwan get a modified MFN-ceiling method where existing duties count toward the cap instead of stacking on top.

USMCA bilateral negotiations resume in Mexico City — the first talks since the Administration signaled it would not renew the agreement. No ag rate changes announced; Canada/Mexico access (top two US ag export destinations) rides on the outcome.

25% tariff on Brazilian goods, including ethanol, announced the prior week following a Section 301 investigation. Inbound tariff: Brazilian ethanol had been gaining US market share — this structurally improves US corn ethanol's domestic position.

Reported deal to unwind the last ag levy: the US would end its 10% fentanyl tariff and China would reciprocate by dropping its 10% tax on US agricultural goods, targeted at cargoes ARRIVING AFTER OCTOBER 1 — timed to when China normally shifts from Brazilian to US supply. China's Ministry of Commerce confirmed the agreement; USTR had not confirmed it at the time of reporting. This is the levy that keeps US soybeans near 13%, so it is the single line item on this page most worth watching.

The Administration signals it will not renew USMCA and will instead open new negotiations. House Ag Democrats and ag groups flag the risk: tariff-free access hits corn, beef, pork, and dairy before anything else.

USTR proposes Section 301 'forced labor' tariffs of 10-12.5% on 59 countries and the EU, with some agricultural exemptions (Annex A). Public comment runs to July 6, hearing July 7 — timed to maintain duties after the Section 122 surcharge expires around July 24.

US-China deal during President Trump's state visit: China to buy at least $17B/yr in US agricultural products through 2028 (in addition to the Oct 2025 soybean commitments) and resumes purchases of US beef and poultry.

US Court of International Trade rules the Section 122 global 10% surcharge (Proclamation 11012) invalid for failing to identify the required balance-of-payments deficit (Oregon v. United States; Burlap & Barrel v. United States). The ruling is under appeal and does not automatically halt collections.

Section 122 global tariff takes effect at 10% (administration announced intent to raise to 15%) after the IEEPA tariffs were terminated. The 150-day statutory clock runs to roughly July 24, 2026 unless Congress extends it.

US Supreme Court rules 6-3 in Learning Resources v. Trump that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs; the April 2025 reciprocal and fentanyl tariffs are voided. The administration pivots to Section 122 the same day.
China lifts the up-to-15% retaliatory ag tariffs from its March 2025 tranche under the Busan agreement, but keeps the broad 10% 'Liberation Day' retaliatory levy — leaving US soybeans at roughly 13%.
Trump-Xi meeting in Busan, South Korea: tariff truce reached. China commits to buy 12 MMT of US soybeans in late 2025 and 25 MMT/yr in 2026-2028; the truce is later extended through Nov 10, 2026.
China imposes first-tranche retaliatory tariffs on US ag (15% on wheat, corn, cotton, chicken; 10% on soybeans, pork, beef, dairy) — later suspended under the Oct 30, 2025 Busan agreement.
